pages.text: "Sheep, up the hill!" Pipo waved his arms behind the flock. But they only grazed and would not move. Today he wanted to herd them to the top alone.
"Aah! Why will you not go?" He stamped and shouted. Startled, sheep scattered everywhere. A lamb hid behind a bush, and his face grew hotter.
All the sheep had fled, leaving the hill empty. Pipo plopped on the grass and gripped it with both hands. "I just wanted to go to the top with the sheep..."
Mom sat close beside him. "Something hot rushed up in your chest, right?" Rubbing his eyes with both hands, he shook his shoulders. "That is anger. Like hill wind, it comes briefly and goes."
"How do I send anger-wind away?" he asked. Mom picked up hay crumbs and set them on her palm. "Blow these away." They waited quietly there.

Mom held her palm before her mouth. "In through the nose—tummy round! Out through the mouth!" Pipo held his palm beside hers and blew. Crumbs fluttered away. His face cooled. "Angry? Blow a big breeze!"
Feeling soft inside, Pipo crept toward the bush. "I am sorry I shouted. I blew all the heat away." The lamb peeped out and rubbed its nose against his hand.
Pipo led slowly. One sheep, two sheep followed in a line. All reached the hilltop! Crouching with hands at his chest, he said, "Blowing out helped!"

One sheep wandered away again. Pipo rested a hand on his belly. "One, hand on tummy! Two, breathe in through the nose! Three, blow out through the mouth!" Puffing his cheeks, he blew. "It is all right. I can try again!"
Mom hugged Pipo and rubbed cheeks. "You know how to blow the heat away!" Anger was not bad. A big breath let it pass. Smiling, he called, "Angry? Blow a big breeze!"
